newsitem.title: USA: Food Lion jury tells judge it deadlocked.
newsitem.headline: Food Lion jury tells judge it deadlocked.

text.p: A jury considering punitive damages in Food Lion Inc.'s lawsuit against the ABC television network and four of its producers sent a second note to the judge late Wednesday saying the panel appeared to be deadlocked.

U.S. District Court Judge Carlton Tilley sent the six-woman, six-man jury home for the night and instructed them to return on Thursday to continue considering punitive damages against ABC over a 1992 hidden-camera investigation of Food Lion's food-handling pracitices.
"Come back with fresh minds in the morning. At that time, I'll give you some additional instructions," Tilley told the jurors.
The latest note said the 12-member jury reached a stalemate because one juror, a woman, was determined not to work with the rest of the panel.
"Judge Tilley, we are truly stuck on further deliberations with the refusal of one juror to take their individual opinion and work collectively with the other jurors," the note said.

"I've tried to help her understand your instructions exactly how they were read. However, determination on her part not to work with us is actually caused a stalemate that would not otherwise exist. Please advise," it continued.
Earlier in the day the jury sent the judge a note indicating that one of the 12 jurors was not cooperating and asked how to proceed.

"It is your duty as jurors to discuss the case with one another in an effort to reach agreement if you can do so. Each of you must decide the case for yourself, but only after full consideration of the evidence with the other members of the jury," the judge responded.
The decision to order punitive damages must be unanimous.

Food Lion sued ABC, owned by Walt Disney Co., and four producers over a hidden camera investigation of its stores in the Carolinas in 1992. The report, which aired on ABC's PrimeTime Live programme, charged Food Lion sold old meat and fish and used unsanitary food handling practices.
A jury hearing the case in U.S. District Court in Greensboro last month awarded the grocery chain $1,400 in compensatory damages.
Food Lion, based in Salisbury, N.C., is a unit of Belgian retailer Ets Delhaize Freres et Cie "LE LION' SA and had 1996 sales of $9 billion.
